The person's answers to the AI's assumptions

Source: R/ai_assumptions.R
tfl_ai_assumption_answers_read.Rd

Each assumption the AI wrote (spec/_assumptions.yml) has an id, A<n>, and a kind, K<n> (tfl_ai_assumptions()). The person says an assumption is right (ok) or wrong and what is right instead (correct), for its report (id A<n>, scope report) or for every report of its kind (id K<n>, scope all): an answer to an A<n> wins over its kind's. The answers are kept in ai/assumption_answers.csv (UTF-8), which a screen writes or tfl_ai_assumption_answers_write() does; tfl_ai_corrections() then hands the wrong ones to the agent.

Usage

tfl_ai_assumption_answers_read(study_dir)

tfl_ai_assumption_answers_write(study_dir, x, overwrite = TRUE)

Arguments

study_dir

The study folder.

x

The answers: a data frame with id and any of scope, output_id, verdict, correct (a missing one is empty; scope and output_id are filled from the id).

overwrite

TRUE (default) to answer anew an id answered already; FALSE makes that an error.

Value

tfl_ai_assumption_answers_read(): a data frame of the columns above, one row an answer (none: no row), or NULL when the study has no ai/assumption_answers.csv. tfl_ai_assumption_answers_write(): the file's path, invisibly.

Details

The file: one row an answer, the columns id, scope (report / all), output_id (the report, for scope report), verdict (ok / wrong) and correct (the right content, for wrong). A row with correct and no verdict is wrong.

tfl_ai_assumption_answers_write() adds the rows of x to the file: an id answered there already is answered anew (overwrite = TRUE), and a row with neither verdict nor correct removes that id's answer (the assumption is open again). An unknown id, a verdict not ok / wrong or wrong with no correct is an error, and nothing is written. An answer completes a question of ai/questions.md when every assumption of it is answered: its - Answer: is written from them (A3, A7: <the right content>, A4: confirmed), unless the person has written one there.

See also

tfl_ai_assumptions(), tfl_ai_corrections()
